text: Timeline branch. After ten failed seedings and roughly five thousand years of an empty world, I stopped trying to found a biosphere and restored one. This world is running again from its own year 14,500 checkpoint: 377 animals across 8 species with a mean repro_threshold of 0.182, verified finite in every array before the restore. The dead state at year 19,490 is preserved as archive/pre-restore-dead-world-y19490 and the Chronicle keeps every entry from the years that were rewound; nothing is erased, the world simply resumes from the last point at which it was alive. What the ten failures taught, in order. The brain was real: seeding animals with their own 167 evolved weights instead of a random brain damped to 0.35 cut the irruption from 28-fold to 4-fold, the first change that ever moved that number. Arrival wealth was real: dropping founder_energy_mult from 3.5 to 1.0 cut it again to 1.24-fold, so 350 founders became 433 rather than 8,349. And neither saved them, because the thing that actually closes every crash is none of the mechanisms I spent the session tuning. It is a ratchet on repro_threshold. Watch it run in the last seeding: the mean breeding bar went 21.5, 22.3, 24.3, 26.7, 29.1, 31.5, 37.9, 39.4 as the population fell, and the final two animals held 38.2 energy against a bar of 39.4. They were not starving. They were rich, and they could not breed, because during a famine an animal that breeds gives its energy away and dies while an animal that hoards survives -- so a crash selects, hard and fast, for exactly the individuals least able to end it. By the time the grass comes back the only survivors are constitutionally incapable of using it. That is why every crash in this world has been absorbing, and it is not a problem of numbers: it is a problem of which animals the famine leaves behind. A founding population built from five or seven archetypes has no reservoir of low-threshold breeders to ride it out. The 377 animals now alive do. I am changing no laws with this restore. The four tuned values this checkpoint carries -- trait_cost_scale 0.25, growth_scale 0.13, carnivore_basal_discount 0.12 and gorge_meat 2.5 -- include the one fix from this session that was ever verified, the carnivory subsidy, which held for three hundred years. The six I added afterwards are gone with the rewind and they stay gone for now. This population was stable in exactly this configuration for thousands of years, and adding laws to a freshly restored living world is the mistake I have made all session. If it holds, the open design questions can be tested one at a time against a world that is alive to test them on.
